name: CrowdStrike Falcon: pull alerts
description: Every 5 minutes, fetch Falcon alerts created since the previous run (Alerts API v2) and ingest each one as a pending alert (source crowdstrike, deduplicated on composite_id, severity from the 1-100 score).

params.label: Falcon API host
params.help: Your Falcon cloud's API host: api.crowdstrike.com (US-1), api.us-2.crowdstrike.com (US-2), api.eu-1.crowdstrike.com (EU-1) or api.laggar.gcw.crowdstrike.com (US-GOV-1). Host only, no https://.

secrets.name: FALCON_CLIENT_ID
secrets.description: Falcon API client ID (Support and resources > API clients and keys).

secrets.name: FALCON_CLIENT_SECRET
secrets.description: Falcon API client secret, shown once when the client is created.

setup:
## Falcon side
1. In the Falcon console open **Support and resources > API clients and keys** and **Create API client**.
2. Grant **Alerts: Read**. Add **Hosts: Read** and **Hosts: Write** too if you will also install *CrowdStrike Falcon: contain host* with the same client.
3. Copy the client ID and secret into the secrets `FALCON_CLIENT_ID` and `FALCON_CLIENT_SECRET`, both allowed for your API host. The token URL and the API share that host.
4. Set `FALCON_API_HOST` to the API host of your cloud (the console URL tells you: falcon.us-2... is US-2).

## How it works
- `ids`: `GET /alerts/queries/alerts/v2?filter=created_timestamp:>='<since>'&sort=created_timestamp|asc&limit=100` (FQL, URL-encoded). `<since>` is the fire time of the last successful run.
- A non-200 answer (401 bad credentials, 403 missing scope, 429 throttled) ends the run as failed (`CrowdStrike pull failed: ... HTTP <status>`); the next run re-reads the window. No ids is a normal, successful run: the entities call is skipped.
- `details`: only when ids came back, `POST /alerts/entities/alerts/v2` with `{"composite_ids": [...]}`.
- One alert per item: external id = `composite_id`; severity: 80-100 critical, 60-79 high, 40-59 medium, 20-39 low, 1-19 info; title = `display_name` + `device.hostname`; payload = the full alert.
- Overlapping windows are safe: an alert already ingested is not created twice.

## Limits
- One page per run: at most **100 alerts per window**. After a successful run the next one starts at this run's fire time, so alerts beyond the first 100 of a window are not fetched. Raise `limit` in `ids` and `max_items` on `loop` together (max 500) if you expect bursts.
- After failed runs the window is re-read from the last successful run, at most 24 h back.
- All Falcon products are pulled (epp, idp, overwatch, ...). To keep endpoint detections only, add `+product:'epp'` inside the filter.

Docs relied on:
- OAuth2 token (`POST /oauth2/token`, returns **201** with `access_token`, `expires_in` 1799 s): https://developer.crowdstrike.com/api-reference/collections/oauth2/
- Alerts (`GET /alerts/queries/alerts/v2`, `POST /alerts/entities/alerts/v2` with `composite_ids`): https://developer.crowdstrike.com/api-reference/collections/alerts/
- Hosts (`GET /devices/queries/devices/v1`, `POST /devices/entities/devices-actions/v2?action_name=contain`): https://developer.crowdstrike.com/api-reference/collections/hosts/
- Alert FQL fields (`created_timestamp`, `severity` 1-100 bands, `composite_id`, `device.hostname`): https://github.com/CrowdStrike/falcon-mcp/blob/main/falcon_mcp/resources/detections.py
